faqs.section_title: Supplier of Last Resort (SOLR)
faqs.question: Can a customer end its SOLR contract mid-cycle to move to a new Retail Supplier?
faqs.answer: Yes — with at least ten (10) calendar days' written notice; the SOLR may not impose an exit or pre-termination fee, though a special meter reading (with its own fee) may be conducted.

faqs.section_title: Supplier of Last Resort (SOLR)
faqs.question: How are system loss charges computed for Last Resort Supply?
faqs.answer: Using the same methodology applied to the Captive Market, with all costs of Last Resort Supply disclosed in an unbundled and transparent manner in the customer's bill.

faqs.section_title: Supplier of Last Resort (SOLR)
faqs.question: What obligations does a SOLR have toward the Retail Customers it serves?
faqs.answer: Continue supplying electricity from the effectivity of the switch until the customer terminates the SOLR contract; administer the transfer process (including metering/billing arrangements); and collect and remit all applicable monthly charges to the appropriate entities.

faqs.section_title: Supplier of Last Resort (SOLR)
faqs.question: Can a SOLR file for a higher rate than the standard formula allows?
faqs.answer: Yes — if the standard rate (WESM nodal/PSA price plus 5% premium) is insufficient to cover its SOLR operations, it may file a proposed SOLR Rate with the ERC, subject to ERC approval or determination, including any reasonable return on investment.

faqs.section_title: Supplier of Last Resort (SOLR)
faqs.question: What happens if the DU itself is acting as SOLR and also has its own PSA-related contracts?
faqs.answer: It must ensure that reassignment of its Power Supply Agreements and recovery of related rates comply with Module Q2 of the Omnibus Rules and its BSUP guidelines, avoiding cross-subsidy between its regulated captive business and its SOLR function. 8. Disconnection and Reconnection

faqs.section_title: Disconnection and Reconnection
faqs.question: What must a Retail Supplier do before disconnecting a customer for non-payment?
faqs.answer: Send a written Notice of Disconnection to the customer, copy furnished to the CRB, at least forty-eight (48) hours before the disconnection date.

faqs.section_title: Disconnection and Reconnection
faqs.question: What happens after the 48-hour disconnection notice period lapses without payment?
faqs.answer: The Retail Supplier may send a Request for Disconnection to the CRB, which forwards it to the NSP within twenty-four (24) hours; the NSP must then disconnect within twenty-four (24) hours (excluding weekends, holidays, and outside 8AM-5PM) and notify the CRB.

faqs.section_title: Disconnection and Reconnection
faqs.question: Can a customer avoid disconnection by paying just before the cut-off?
faqs.answer: Yes — if the customer settles in full and presents proof of payment before actual disconnection (unless otherwise agreed), the Retail Supplier must advise the CRB and NSP in writing to desist from disconnecting.

faqs.section_title: Disconnection and Reconnection
faqs.question: Can a Retail Supplier be held liable for a wrongful disconnection?
faqs.answer: Yes — after due process, a Retail Supplier may be held liable if a disconnection did not follow the required procedure, or if it pursued disconnection over an outstanding balance that was actually the subject of a valid billing dispute.

faqs.section_title: Disconnection and Reconnection
faqs.question: What happens if a Retail Supplier itself fails to pay the NSP for wheeling services?
faqs.answer: The NSP sends a written Notice of Disconnection to the CRB stating that supply will be terminated within seven (7) calendar days from the supplier's receipt; if unpaid after 48 hours, the NSP sends a copy of the notice to the affected Retail Customers, who then must enter into a SOLR contract.

faqs.section_title: Disconnection and Reconnection
faqs.question: Can a Retail Supplier invoke a "grace payment" provision more than once for the same unpaid bill?
faqs.answer: No — if the Retail Supplier tenders full payment just before disconnection, the NSP must desist, but the supplier may only invoke this provision once for the same unpaid bill.

faqs.section_title: Disconnection and Reconnection
faqs.question: Who initiates a request for reconnection?
faqs.answer: The entity that originally requested the disconnection — whether a Retail Supplier or an NSP.

faqs.section_title: Disconnection and Reconnection
faqs.question: How quickly must a customer be reconnected after remedying the grounds for disconnection?
faqs.answer: Within twenty-four (24) hours after the customer presents proof to the Retail Supplier that the disconnection grounds (e.g., proof of payment) have been remedied.

faqs.section_title: Disconnection and Reconnection
faqs.question: What happens if multiple suppliers requested disconnection of the same customer?
faqs.answer: Reconnection is only executed once the Primary Retail Supplier has issued the Notice of Reconnection to the NSP.

faqs.section_title: Disconnection and Reconnection
faqs.question: What is the process for reconnection when disconnection was due to a Retail Supplier's non-payment to the NSP?
faqs.answer: The NSP issues a Notice of Reconnection to the CRB, copy furnished the Retail Supplier; the CRB forwards it to the customer, and the customer retains the right to continue with its supplier (or SOLR) until an RSC with a new supplier is approved.

faqs.section_title: Disconnection and Reconnection
faqs.question: Under what circumstances may disconnection be deferred?
faqs.answer: If the outstanding amount is settled before the scheduled disconnection; the Retail Supplier recalls the notice due to a special payment or restructuring agreement; the supplier recalls it for another valid reason; or the ERC/a lawful authority issues a stay order after notice and hearing.

faqs.section_title: Disconnection and Reconnection
faqs.question: Does a deferred disconnection erase the customer's underlying liabilities?
faqs.answer: No — the customer remains liable for any outstanding obligations under ERC issuances, WESM Rules, and existing retail contracts, notwithstanding the deferment.

faqs.section_title: Disconnection and Reconnection
faqs.question: On what days is disconnection prohibited, even with a valid notice?
faqs.answer: On any Saturday, Sunday, or public holiday, and on any other day outside 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM.

faqs.section_title: Disconnection and Reconnection
faqs.question: What household circumstance can suspend a disconnection, even after proper notice?
faqs.answer: If any occupant is dependent on a life-support system requiring electricity, evidenced by a medical certificate from a licensed physician or public health official; suspension applies only during the dependency period and cannot exceed two (2) months.

faqs.section_title: Disconnection and Reconnection
faqs.question: What if a customer never actually received its Statement of Account?
faqs.answer: Disconnection may be suspended if the customer proves it did not receive the Statement of Account from the Retail Supplier or SOLR — but not simply because the customer refused to accept the bill.

faqs.section_title: Disconnection and Reconnection
faqs.question: What if a customer is billed a lump sum for several unpaid billing cycles at once?
faqs.answer: Disconnection may be suspended if this occurred due to the supplier's or SOLR's failure to issue timely bills, provided the customer pays the current bill on its due date and enters a staggered payment scheme spanning the number of unpaid months.

faqs.section_title: Disconnection and Reconnection
faqs.question: Can a DU or NSP disconnect without any prior written notice?
faqs.answer: Yes, but only if a dangerous or hazardous condition arises; the NSP must still notify affected end-users after the fact, and service is restored only once the hazard has been addressed.

faqs.section_title: Disconnection and Reconnection
faqs.question: What obligations continue even after a customer is validly disconnected?
faqs.answer: Any disconnection is without prejudice to charges, interest, or penalties that may still be legally imposed on the disconnected customer.

faqs.section_title: Disconnection and Reconnection
faqs.question: Do the disconnection rules for SOLR customers differ materially from regular Retail Supplier disconnections?
faqs.answer: The core mechanics are similar (48-hour notice, CRB routing, 24-hour execution windows), but SOLR disconnections specifically require the RMSP to execute the CRB's forwarded request within twenty-four (24) hours and bar reconnection until all SOLR obligations are settled.

faqs.section_title: Disconnection and Reconnection
faqs.question: What existing rules govern disconnection procedures beyond the Omnibus Rules themselves?
faqs.answer: The NSP's existing internal rules and other relevant ERC and DOE issuances continue to apply alongside the specific disconnection/reconnection timelines set in Module H. 9. Retail Aggregation Program (RAP)

faqs.section_title: Retail Aggregation Program (RAP)
faqs.question: What is the fundamental purpose of the Retail Aggregation Program?
faqs.answer: RAP allows smaller end-users, whose individual demand does not meet the CREM eligibility threshold on its own, to pool their demand together as an Aggregated Group so they can collectively qualify to switch to a Retail Supplier.

faqs.section_title: Retail Aggregation Program (RAP)
faqs.question: Can an end-user that already qualifies for CREM individually still join an Aggregated Group?
faqs.answer: No — an end-user that has already reached the eligibility threshold on its own, or is already a CREM End-user, may not participate in RAP.

faqs.section_title: Retail Aggregation Program (RAP)
faqs.question: What must a Retail Supplier do once it has pooled the demand of at least two end-users?
faqs.answer: Serve written notice on the concerned DU that an Aggregated Group has been formed, including relevant customer information, at least ninety (90) calendar days before the intended switch date.

faqs.section_title: Retail Aggregation Program (RAP)
faqs.question: What is the DU's role once notified of a new Aggregated Group?
faqs.answer: It must, in a non-discriminatory manner, assist and ensure the derived aggregated demand computation is properly validated consistent with Module D4.

faqs.section_title: Retail Aggregation Program (RAP)
faqs.question: How is an Aggregated Group billed under RAP?
faqs.answer: Module F on Billing and Payments applies fully to RAP; for aggregation through a Virtual Meter in the WESM, each Aggregated Member gets its own billing statement reflecting its proportional share of wheeling charges.

faqs.section_title: Retail Aggregation Program (RAP)
faqs.question: Can a Retail Supplier impose special fees on just one Aggregated Member?
faqs.answer: Only if that specific condition is clearly disclosed and provided for in the RSC — undisclosed fees or conditions may not be imposed unilaterally.

faqs.section_title: Retail Aggregation Program (RAP)
faqs.question: Who is responsible for credit and collection matters within an Aggregated Group?
faqs.answer: The Retail Supplier is responsible for credit and collection concerning each Aggregated Member, who must remit payment per agreed terms; one member's non-payment does not prejudice the others.

faqs.section_title: Retail Aggregation Program (RAP)
faqs.question: Can a Retail Supplier disconnect the whole Aggregated Group because one member did not pay?
faqs.answer: No — it cannot request disconnection of the entire aggregated group due to non-payment by one member, though it retains the right to pursue other RSC remedies against that specific member.

faqs.section_title: Retail Aggregation Program (RAP)
faqs.question: What are the key responsibilities of Aggregated Group members?
faqs.answer: Communicating, transacting, and paying the Retail Supplier; selecting and evaluating among ERC-licensed suppliers; providing information the supplier reasonably requires; reviewing the RSC's disclosure statement; and meeting any applicable WESM requirements.

faqs.section_title: Retail Aggregation Program (RAP)
faqs.question: What happens if one Aggregated Member commits pilferage or breaches its contract?
faqs.answer: Provided there is no condonation, collusion, or conspiracy among members, disconnection may be implemented only against the erring member; the Aggregated Group as a whole continues to exist notwithstanding that one member's disconnection.

faqs.section_title: Retail Aggregation Program (RAP)
faqs.question: Is there a maximum number of members allowed in an Aggregated Group?
faqs.answer: No — there is no cap on the number of end-users that may form an Aggregated Group, so long as their combined demand meets the prevailing eligibility threshold and they satisfy the Contiguous Area requirement.

faqs.section_title: Retail Aggregation Program (RAP)
faqs.question: Can Aggregated Members later decide they want separate, individual contracts instead of one group contract?
faqs.answer: Yes — while the Retail Supplier may execute a single RSC for the whole Aggregated Group, members may opt for individual contracts instead, provided the terms and conditions remain identical across all such contracts. 10. Redistribution in the Retail Market (Condominiums and Complexes)

faqs.section_title: Redistribution in the Retail Market (Condominiums and Complexes)
faqs.question: What is "redistribution" in the context of the Retail Market?
faqs.answer: It is the arrangement where the owner, administrator, or homeowners' association of a building/complex — whose single revenue meter meets the CREM threshold — switches to CREM as a "CREM End-user Redistributor" and then resells/redistributes electricity to individual sub-metered occupants within that building or complex.

faqs.section_title: Redistribution in the Retail Market (Condominiums and Complexes)
faqs.question: Once it becomes a CREM End-user Redistributor, what rights and obligations does the redistributor take on?
faqs.answer: All the same rights and obligations of an ordinary CREM End-user under the Omnibus Rules, in addition to its specific redistribution obligations toward its unit-owners/tenants.

faqs.section_title: Redistribution in the Retail Market (Condominiums and Complexes)
faqs.question: Can a CREM End-user Redistributor profit from redistributing electricity to its tenants or unit-owners?
faqs.answer: No — unit-owners/users only pay for their actual sub-metered consumption at a rate no higher than what the RES charges, and at no point may the redistributor derive profit from this recovery, including recovery of common-area consumption estimates.

faqs.section_title: Redistribution in the Retail Market (Condominiums and Complexes)
faqs.question: How are non-technical losses handled in a redistribution setup?
faqs.answer: Reasonable expenses may be recovered by the redistributor, but non-technical losses (e.g., pilferage-related losses) must be recovered pursuant to Republic Act No. 7832 (the Anti-Pilferage Law), the Revised Penal Code, and other related laws — not simply passed on at will.

faqs.section_title: Redistribution in the Retail Market (Condominiums and Complexes)
faqs.question: Who bears the cost of sub-meters installed for individual units?
faqs.answer: The CREM End-user Redistributor must provide and install the sub-meters, and this cost cannot be charged or passed on to the individual lessees/unit-users.

faqs.section_title: Redistribution in the Retail Market (Condominiums and Complexes)
faqs.question: What standards must sub-meters meet before installation?
faqs.answer: All watt-hour meters, including sub-meters, must be tested, certified, and sealed by the ERC prior to installation, following the Rules and Procedures for the Test and Maintenance of Electric Meters of Distribution Utilities.

faqs.section_title: Redistribution in the Retail Market (Condominiums and Complexes)
faqs.question: How should common areas be metered in a redistribution setup?
faqs.answer: Common areas should be metered separately from individual units; if building design makes this impossible, consumption may be estimated using a method agreed upon by the redistributor and unit-owners/users, again without the redistributor profiting from that recovery.

faqs.section_title: Redistribution in the Retail Market (Condominiums and Complexes)
faqs.question: What are the deposit rules for individual unit-owners/users under a CREM End-user Redistributor?
faqs.answer: Deposit and refund requirements follow the Magna Carta for Residential Electricity Consumers and the DSOAR; the bill deposit equals the estimated monthly billing, adjusted annually if actual billing changes by more than 10%, with interest credited yearly at the BSP Peso Savings Account rate (or ERC-approved equivalent).

faqs.section_title: Redistribution in the Retail Market (Condominiums and Complexes)
faqs.question: Must rebates from the Retail Supplier or NSP be passed on to unit-owners?
faqs.answer: Yes — rebates and refunds from the Retail Supplier or NSP must be passed on to unit-owners/users, computed and allocated in the same manner used by the NSP.

faqs.section_title: Redistribution in the Retail Market (Condominiums and Complexes)
faqs.question: What additional conditions apply to a CREM End-user Redistributor operating a substation?
faqs.answer: It must own the substation and connected buildings; the substation/buildings must sit within a single, contiguous fenced-off industrial or commercial complex; other-owned buildings inside the complex need NSP consent to connect (or must be served directly by the franchised NSP); a valid NSP contract must define the substation's maximum load capacity; and a revenue meter must be installed in each connected building.

faqs.section_title: Redistribution in the Retail Market (Condominiums and Complexes)
faqs.question: What rights do individual unit-owners/users have under a redistribution arrangement?
faqs.answer: The same key consumer rights given to residential customers under the Magna Carta for Residential Electricity Consumers — including refund of bill deposits and overbillings, ERC meter testing, due process and prior notice before disconnection, payment under protest, service despite a prior tenant's arrears, reconnection rights, and the right to file ERC complaints — plus the right to inspect the RES's billing to the redistributor.

faqs.section_title: Redistribution in the Retail Market (Condominiums and Complexes)
faqs.question: What obligations do unit-owners/users have under a redistribution arrangement?
faqs.answer: To pay any required bill/security deposit (or their proportionate share of one); to pay bills on time per their contract or the redistributor/HOA's policies; to pay late charges/penalties as disclosed; and to allow accurate recording of consumption on their sub-meter.

faqs.section_title: Redistribution in the Retail Market (Condominiums and Complexes)
faqs.question: Can a homeowners' association decide to revert a condominium building from CREM back to the Captive Market?
faqs.answer: Yes, subject to a formal resolution or agreement stating its intent, exercised at least three (3) months before the RSC's expiry; failure to notify within this window means the building continues in CREM by default, and non-compliance can be a ground to disallow future reversion requests. 11. Reversion to the Captive Market

faqs.section_title: Reversion to the Captive Market
faqs.question: Can a CREM End-user simply decide to go back to being a captive customer at will?
faqs.answer: Generally no — once migrated to CREM, a customer normally cannot revert. An exception exists if its average monthly peak demand drops below twenty-five percent (25%) of the prevailing CREM threshold for six consecutive months (not due to seasonal factors), allowing it to request ERC-approved reversion.

faqs.section_title: Reversion to the Captive Market
faqs.question: What must a CREM End-user do to request reversion for sustained low demand?
faqs.answer: Send a written request to the ERC with confirmation from its Retail Supplier or SOLR that its demand has decreased by the required amount; upon ERC approval, it must settle its obligations under the RSC/SOLR contract before the Retail Supplier/SOLR informs the CRB and ERC of the reversion.

faqs.section_title: Reversion to the Captive Market
faqs.question: What is the reversion threshold for GEOP End-users?
faqs.answer: If a GEOP End-user's average monthly peak demand falls to at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the prevailing GEOP threshold for six consecutive months (not seasonal), the RE Supplier sends a written request to the DU (with RMSP confirmation), and the customer is reverted to the Captive Market.

faqs.section_title: Reversion to the Captive Market
faqs.question: How often can a GEOP End-user exercise the option to revert to captive status?
faqs.answer: Only once every twenty-four (24) months.

faqs.section_title: Reversion to the Captive Market
faqs.question: How is a returning GEOP End-user treated by the DU upon reversion?
faqs.answer: As a new customer — meaning it goes through the DU's standard new-connection/new-customer processes rather than simply resuming its old captive account.

faqs.section_title: Reversion to the Captive Market
faqs.question: Can an individual Aggregated Member simply opt out of its Aggregated Group mid-contract?
faqs.answer: No — in no case may an Aggregated Member opt out of the Aggregated Group during the term of its contract.

faqs.section_title: Reversion to the Captive Market
faqs.question: What acts of default by a Retail Supplier let an Aggregated Group terminate its contract?
faqs.answer: Breach of confidentiality over member information; excess billing of the contracted rate (without immediate correction); revocation of WESM membership; non-payment to the DU/Generation Company/WESM; a final court conviction for fraud or deceit; an LRSE attributable to the supplier; or any other circumstance the ERC deems an act of default.

faqs.section_title: Reversion to the Captive Market
faqs.question: If a Retail Supplier is in default, can the Aggregated Group leave immediately without further supply?
faqs.answer: The Group may revert to the Captive Market (individually or as a group), but the defaulting Retail Supplier must continue supplying electricity under the same RSC terms until the reversion or switch to another supplier actually takes effect.

faqs.section_title: Reversion to the Captive Market
faqs.question: How much notice must an Aggregated Group give the DU to revert by mutual agreement (not due to default)?
faqs.answer: Thirty (30) calendar days before the effectivity of the termination, whether reverting individually or as a group.

faqs.section_title: Reversion to the Captive Market
faqs.question: Does a special meter reading apply when an Aggregated Group's contract ends?
faqs.answer: Yes — a special meter reading may be conducted on a date other than the regular reading date, with an additional fee charged by the RMSP to whichever party requested the service. 12. Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: Where can a Retail Supplier legally market its services?
faqs.answer: Any Retail Supplier except a Local RES may market anywhere in the Philippines where the WESM is already implemented. A Local RES may only market within its own Franchise Area.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: Is a Retail Supplier liable for the misconduct of its sales agents?
faqs.answer: Yes — a Retail Supplier is always responsible and liable for the conduct of its employees, officers, and authorized representatives (whether internal or third-party), and any violation by them is treated as a violation by the supplier itself.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: What basic standards must a Retail Supplier follow during marketing?
faqs.answer: Comply with all applicable laws; avoid misleading, deceptive, or unfair conduct; avoid undue pressure, harassment, or coercion; give customers at least one business day to review documents; use clear, explicitly defined terms; and ensure any comparisons made are clear, accurate, timely, and not missing important information.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: Can a salesperson make verbal promises about contract terms that are not written down?
faqs.answer: No — a Retail Supplier must not make verbal representations about contracts, rights, or obligations unless those representations are also contained in a written offer.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: Can a Retail Supplier claim it has "special relations" with a DU to win over a customer?
faqs.answer: No — it must not state or imply that it or its Affiliate has special relationships or preferential status with a DU, and must not solicit preferential treatment from a DU for its customers or affiliated generators.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: When is a Retail Supplier prohibited from calling or visiting a customer for marketing purposes?
faqs.answer: At any time on a Saturday, Sunday, or public holiday, or on any other day outside 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM — unless otherwise mutually agreed in writing.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: What must a salesperson disclose at the start of any marketing contact?
faqs.answer: The name of the salesperson, the name of the Retail Supplier, and its RES License number (or proof of authorization as a Local RES).

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: What contact details must be given to a customer before completing a marketing contact?
faqs.answer: Business address, telephone number, mobile number, and email address, whether the contact is in person, in writing, or electronic.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: Must a Retail Supplier maintain a phone number and website?
faqs.answer: Yes — it must have a working telephone number and an interactive website accessible to the general public.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: What conduct standard applies to in-person marketing visits?
faqs.answer: The Retail Supplier or its salespersons must exercise due care and respect toward the customer's property and premises when visiting in person.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: What must happen if a customer refuses or asks to end a marketing contact?
faqs.answer: The Retail Supplier must immediately comply and refrain from initiating another transaction with that customer for at least twenty (20) business days from the date of the request, unless the customer advises otherwise.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: How long must "No Disturbance Requests" be honored?
faqs.answer: At all times, unless the customer itself revokes the request.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: What training must a Retail Supplier provide its sales staff?
faqs.answer: Training ensuring staff comply with applicable rules, can clearly explain pricing/billing/eligibility factors and comparisons with competitors, and emphasize the need for customers to give informed consent to an RSC — with continuing training/evaluation, three-year record retention, and an annual training report to the ERC.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: What are the rules for advertising the price of electricity?
faqs.answer: Advertising must not be misleading or deceptive; must fairly and verifiably compare offers; and must provide contact information for pricing inquiries. If quoting a proposed price, it must state the offer's validity period, contract duration, how a variable price will be determined, or the per-kWh price over the contract term.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: What must a Retail Supplier disclose when advertising the price of electricity specifically?
faqs.answer: It must disclose bill components such as the DU's Wheeling Charges and clarify that the RES Charge is only part of the customer's Total Bill — preventing customers from mistaking the supplier's rate for the entire electricity price.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: Must a building/condo administrator disclose whether tenants are captive or retail customers?
faqs.answer: Yes — a CREM End-user Redistributor administering a leased residential/commercial/industrial property must disclose its current end-user/meter classification to prospective lessees or unit-users.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: How confidential must customer information be kept by a Retail Supplier?
faqs.answer: It must be treated as confidential and used only for the purpose for which it was obtained; it cannot be disclosed without the customer's written consent, except to comply with a legal requirement or when referring past-due accounts to a debt collection agency.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: Can a customer request a copy of all information a Retail Supplier holds about it?
faqs.answer: Yes — free of charge, including metering data, upon the customer's request.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: What marketing-contact records must a Retail Supplier keep, and for how long?
faqs.answer: All marketing contacts over the previous three (3) years (names, dates, times, staff involved, email exchanges); all "No Disturbance Requests" over the previous twelve (12) months; and all refused/terminated contacts over the previous three (3) years — subject to ERC verification via regulatory visits.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: How long must Retail Supply Contracts and Power Supply Agreements be kept on file?
faqs.answer: All executed RSCs (active or not) and all Power Supply Agreements with Generation Companies must be documented for a period of three (3) years.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: What ethical standard governs how Retail Suppliers handle market information?
faqs.answer: They must ensure information disclosed to media/publications/surveys is accurate and not misleading, and must strictly follow procedures ensuring transparent, properly documented transactions with no concealment or misrepresentation.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: What is an "Offer Sheet" and when must it be given to a prospective customer?
faqs.answer: It is the document presented during the initial proposal stage, showing pricing structure, contract price, obligations, and charges consistent with what will appear in the eventual signed RSC — it must be given before the customer decides to enter an RSC.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: List some of the minimum provisions that must be explicitly stated in every RSC.
faqs.answer: Full contact details of the supplier; billing type/frequency and payment methods; all applicable prices/charges (inclusive of all costs); price-adjustment mechanisms for variable pricing; additional charges/penalties for late payment/default; cash security deposit terms; termination circumstances; early-termination charges and calculation method; cooling-off cancellation rights; complaint-handling procedures; SOLR transfer circumstances; and agreed allowable outage hours.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: How is an Offer Sheet considered "received" by a customer?
faqs.answer: On personal delivery, the delivery date; if emailed on/before 5:00 PM on a business day, that business day; if emailed after 5:00 PM, the next business day; otherwise, the day it is actually received.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: How soon after the Offer Sheet is received can a Retail Supplier sign an RSC with the customer?
faqs.answer: Within five (5) business days from the date of receipt of the Offer Sheet by the customer.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: Can a Retail Supplier supply electricity without ever having the customer sign a formal RSC?
faqs.answer: No — an Offer Sheet alone, even if signed, does not satisfy the RSC requirement; no supplier may supply electricity to a customer without a duly signed RSC, a copy of which must be given to the customer.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: Can an RSC take effect before the Cooling-off Period expires?
faqs.answer: No, not unless both parties otherwise agree — supply must commence on the agreed day, but not earlier than expiration of the Cooling-off Period.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: Can contract rates or terms be changed unilaterally by the Retail Supplier?
faqs.answer: No — the rates, terms, and conditions of an RSC may only be modified by written agreement of both contracting parties; however, price changes that automatically follow a previously agreed written formula do not require a fresh agreement.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: Can a Retail Supplier automatically renew a contract without telling the customer?
faqs.answer: Only if the original RSC contains an automatic renewal clause, and the supplier notifies the customer at least sixty (60) calendar days before expiry; failure to notify invalidates the automatic renewal clause, though the parties may still choose to enter a new contract.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: If a templated RSC contains an ambiguous clause, how should it be interpreted?
faqs.answer: Liberally in favor of the Retail Customer and strictly against the Retail Supplier.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: How long is the standard Cooling-off Period, and can a customer waive it?
faqs.answer: Five (5) business days (or longer, if agreed) from the date of signing; a customer may waive this right, but must otherwise give written cancellation notice received by the supplier within the five-day window to exercise it.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: Does the Cooling-off Period apply again every time an RSC is renewed?
faqs.answer: No — the Cooling-off Period no longer applies to renewals of existing RSCs.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: What must a DU do to keep its Local RES and Affiliate RES operationally separate?
faqs.answer: Maintain separate financial records and books of accounts, ensure operational, accounting, and financial separation, and only share assets/equipment under specific ERC-approved conditions (per ERC Resolution No. 02, Series of 2007), never sharing databases, information, or costs between regulated and non-regulated segments.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: Can a DU give its own Local RES or Affiliate RES preferential treatment in connections or metering?
faqs.answer: No — the DU must not favor its Local/Affiliate RES over other Retail Suppliers in distribution connection, system maintenance, meter installation/testing/repair, or meter reading.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: Can a Local RES use the DU's brand name freely?
faqs.answer: A Local RES must use, in addition to the DU's business name/trademark/logo, another distinguishing name or symbol identifying it as the Local RES of that DU; the DU's Affiliate RES, by contrast, cannot use the DU's name/brand at all.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: Can a DU promote its Affiliate RES's electricity offers when a customer calls asking general questions?
faqs.answer: No — the DU must not promote its Local/Affiliate RES or comment on any supplier, and must instead direct the customer to the ERC website for the list of licensed RES/authorized Local RES, without making negative remarks about competitors.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: Can a DU staff member sit in on a sales conversation between a customer and an RES?
faqs.answer: No — the DU may only participate in meetings on technical/operational distribution matters, in the same manner it does with non-affiliate RES, and must never listen to or participate in a sales discussion between a customer and any RES (affiliated or not).

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: Can a DU share distribution-system information with its own Affiliate RES that it does not share with competitors?
faqs.answer: No — information a DU obtains through its regulated business cannot be shared with its Local/Affiliate RES unless equally made available, on the same terms, to other Retail Suppliers operating in its franchise area.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: Can a DU subsidize or guarantee loans for its Affiliate RES?
faqs.answer: No — a DU may not subsidize its Local/Affiliate RES's business in any manner, and may not finance, co-sign, or guarantee any loan or financial obligation of its Affiliate RES.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: If a DU charges its Affiliate RES for shared services, how must that fee be set?
faqs.answer: Based on market price — essentially what the DU would charge any other Retail Supplier for the same services, products, property, equipment, or facilities.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: What must a Retail Supplier's Complaint Handling Procedures (CHP) cover, at minimum?
faqs.answer: How complaints are filed; the process and timelines for handling and resolving them; the method of response (e.g., in writing); and the right to escalate unresolved complaints to the ERC or the regular courts, board, or tribunal.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: When must a new Retail Supplier submit its Complaint Handling Procedures to the ERC?
faqs.answer: Within twenty (20) calendar days of the issuance of its RES License or Letter-authority, and the CHP must appear in all its executed RSCs thereafter.

faqs.section_title: Code of Conduct for Retail Market Participants
faqs.question: How long must a Retail Supplier keep records of customer complaints?
faqs.answer: At least three (3) years after each complaint has been resolved, including the customer's details, the complaint, how and when it was handled, the resolution, and the reasons for it — made available to the ERC upon request. 13. Magna Carta for Retail Customers — Rights and Obligations

faqs.section_title: Magna Carta for Retail Customers — Rights and Obligations
faqs.question: What is the "Magna Carta for Retail Customers"?
faqs.answer: It is Module M of the Omnibus Rules, a bill of rights (and corresponding obligations) specifically for Retail Customers, covering everything from choice of supplier to due process before disconnection.

faqs.section_title: Magna Carta for Retail Customers — Rights and Obligations
faqs.question: What is a Retail Customer's most fundamental right under the Magna Carta?
faqs.answer: The Right to Choose its Supplier of Electricity, whether sourced from conventional or renewable technology, among ERC-licensed or authorized Retail Suppliers — including the right of a prospective lessee/unit-user to be informed of a building's end-user/meter classification.

faqs.section_title: Magna Carta for Retail Customers — Rights and Obligations
faqs.question: What is the Right to Non-Discriminatory and Non-Preferential Services?
faqs.answer: The right to receive Distribution Wheeling Services or Transmission Services from the NSP on the same basis as captive or directly connected customers, and to have equal opportunity to avail of Retail Supplier products/services on the same basis as affiliated customers.

faqs.section_title: Magna Carta for Retail Customers — Rights and Obligations
faqs.question: What options does a customer have if it disagrees with its RSC or a bill?
faqs.answer: The Right to Dispute its RSC, Electricity Bills, and File a Complaint before the ERC — first through the supplier's Complaint Handling Procedures, then, if unresolved, through intermediation or a Dispute Resolution Case before the ERC or regular courts/tribunals.

faqs.section_title: Magna Carta for Retail Customers — Rights and Obligations
faqs.question: What does the Right to Transparent Billing guarantee?
faqs.answer: The right to receive a bill containing clear and complete information as prescribed in Module F (Billing and Payments), so the customer can verify exactly what it is being charged for.

faqs.section_title: Magna Carta for Retail Customers — Rights and Obligations
faqs.question: When can a customer negotiate the terms of its RSC, such as a pre-termination fee?
faqs.answer: In cases of pre-termination of the RSC (whether initiated by the customer or the supplier), the customer has the Right to Negotiate the Terms and Conditions of its RSC, including the pre-termination fee amount.

faqs.section_title: Magna Carta for Retail Customers — Rights and Obligations
faqs.question: What is the Right to Refuse a Marketing Contact?
faqs.answer: A customer may refuse any marketing contact initiated by a supplier; upon refusal, the supplier must immediately comply and refrain from initiating another transaction, unless the customer later advises or revokes the refusal.

faqs.section_title: Magna Carta for Retail Customers — Rights and Obligations
faqs.question: What information can a customer demand from its Retail Supplier free of charge?
faqs.answer: The Right to Information — details of all customer information the supplier holds, including historical metered quantities and energy consumption, at no cost.

faqs.section_title: Magna Carta for Retail Customers — Rights and Obligations
faqs.question: Can a Retail Supplier terminate an RSC while it is under dispute, just to avoid its obligations?
faqs.answer: No — under the Right to Protection Against Premature Termination, suppliers must refrain from arbitrary premature termination, especially of RSCs under dispute or subject to a Cease and Desist Order, and are subject to the same termination-fee penalties they would impose on customers if found at fault.

faqs.section_title: Magna Carta for Retail Customers — Rights and Obligations
faqs.question: When and how may a DU disconnect a Retail Customer's electricity service?
faqs.answer: Only after a valid 48-hour prior notice for legitimate reasons (e.g., non-payment or RSC violations), and never on a Saturday, Sunday, public holiday, or outside 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM — this is the Right to Due Process Prior to Disconnection.

faqs.section_title: Magna Carta for Retail Customers — Rights and Obligations
faqs.question: How confidential is a customer's personal and demand information?
faqs.answer: Under the Right to Confidential Treatment of Customer Information, it must be kept confidential except when the ERC or DOE requires disclosure for market monitoring under their respective rules.

faqs.section_title: Magna Carta for Retail Customers — Rights and Obligations
faqs.question: How quickly must a security deposit be returned to a customer after service ends?
faqs.answer: Within thirty (30) calendar days from termination of service (unless a shorter period is agreed in writing), provided the customer has no outstanding balance — this is the Right to Return of Security Deposits.

faqs.section_title: Magna Carta for Retail Customers — Rights and Obligations
faqs.question: What is "payment under protest" and when can a customer use it?
faqs.answer: It is the right to pay a disputed bill (e.g., from a billing adjustment due to meter stoppage, or a differential billing for alleged illegal use) in order to maintain continuous supply, without this payment being treated as an admission of the supplier's claims — while the customer can still pursue its complaint separately.

faqs.section_title: Magna Carta for Retail Customers — Rights and Obligations
faqs.question: Can a customer switch suppliers if it still owes money on a disputed bill?
faqs.answer: Yes — the Right to Switch to Another Retail Supplier allows this, provided the outstanding balance is based on charges not expressly identified in the RSC (consistent with Module E1.4).

faqs.section_title: Magna Carta for Retail Customers — Rights and Obligations
faqs.question: What is a customer's core payment obligation?
faqs.answer: To pay its electricity bills promptly, based on the period stipulated in the RSC, DWSA/TSA, or the due date reflected on its regular billing statement.

faqs.section_title: Magna Carta for Retail Customers — Rights and Obligations
faqs.question: Must a customer accept delivery of its monthly bill?
faqs.answer: Yes — customers (and unit-owners/users under redistribution) must accept their monthly bills, without prejudice to their rights to dispute charges or pay under protest.

faqs.section_title: Magna Carta for Retail Customers — Rights and Obligations
faqs.question: What must a customer do before signing an RSC?
faqs.answer: Properly review and analyze the terms and conditions, including the contract price, electricity price, other applicable charges, and any amendments, so it fully understands what it is agreeing to.

faqs.section_title: Magna Carta for Retail Customers — Rights and Obligations
faqs.question: What access must a customer allow to NSP/RMSP personnel?
faqs.answer: Access to authorized, properly identified employees or representatives for inspection, installation, reading, testing, repairs, removal, and disconnection purposes, as needed.

faqs.section_title: Magna Carta for Retail Customers — Rights and Obligations
faqs.question: What is strictly prohibited under the "Obligation Not to Commit Any Illegal Use of Electricity"?
faqs.answer: Any act resulting in pilferage of electricity, whether or not it involves tampering with meters.

faqs.section_title: Magna Carta for Retail Customers — Rights and Obligations
faqs.question: Does the Magna Carta apply to unit-owners/lessees under a CREM End-user Redistributor arrangement too?
faqs.answer: Yes — many of the same rights (e.g., refund of deposits, payment under protest, right to switch in billing disputes) extend by reference to individual unit-owners/users in redistribution setups, on top of the specific protections in Module J.

faqs.section_title: Magna Carta for Retail Customers — Rights and Obligations
faqs.question: Can a customer be charged extra fees not mentioned anywhere in its RSC?
faqs.answer: No — the RSC must clearly and previously disclose any late payment, penalty, administrative, or other charges before they may be collected; undisclosed charges cannot be imposed.

faqs.section_title: Magna Carta for Retail Customers — Rights and Obligations
faqs.question: What recourse does a customer have if it feels marketing conduct was abusive?
faqs.answer: It may lodge a complaint via the supplier's Complaint Handling Procedures and, if unresolved, escalate the matter to the ERC, which has original and exclusive jurisdiction over Retail Market disputes.

faqs.section_title: Magna Carta for Retail Customers — Rights and Obligations
faqs.question: Are these rights only available to CREM customers, or also GEOP and RAP participants?
faqs.answer: The Magna Carta in Module M applies broadly to "Retail Customers," a term that covers CREM End-users, GEOP End-users, Directly Connected Customers, and Aggregated Groups alike.

faqs.section_title: Magna Carta for Retail Customers — Rights and Obligations
faqs.question: Why does the Omnibus Rules dedicate an entire module solely to customer rights?
faqs.answer: Because one of the ERC's stated objectives in adopting the Omnibus Rules (Module A2.1(e)) is to strengthen consumer protection against abuse of market power and discriminatory or anti-competitive behavior — Module M operationalizes that objective into enforceable, itemized rights. 14. Reportorial Requirements

faqs.section_title: Reportorial Requirements
faqs.question: Why do NSPs, SOLRs, Retail Suppliers, and the CRB have to file periodic reports with the ERC?
faqs.answer: Module N requires ongoing reportorial submissions so the ERC can monitor market activity, verify compliance, track switching and pricing trends, and support informed policymaking, all submitted through the CREM-Monitoring and Reporting System (CREM-MRS).

faqs.section_title: Reportorial Requirements
faqs.question: What must an NSP report to the ERC every month?
faqs.answer: A monthly report (due the 20th of the following month) on end-users by average monthly peak demand threshold, including aggregated group/customer name, retail category, billing address, meter/account number, twelve months of historical usage, and customer contact information.

faqs.section_title: Reportorial Requirements
faqs.question: What semi-annual report must an NSP file regarding switching compliance?
faqs.answer: A semi-annual report (due every July 30 and January 31) showing compliance with the twenty (20)-day requirement to complete switching procedures such as CA and DWSA/TSA execution.

faqs.section_title: Reportorial Requirements
faqs.question: What must an NSP report if customer migration is straining its supply?
faqs.answer: A report within thirty (30) days of determining actual or forecasted stranding of supply caused by migration to the Retail Market, including mitigation efforts, projected rate impact, and estimated rate impact after mitigation, per Module

faqs.section_title: Getting Started — Understanding the Retail Electricity Market
faqs.question: Q325. What quarterly reports must a SOLR submit?
faqs.answer: A report on contracted capacity/energy with generation companies and intended SOLR allocations (due the 20th of the month after each quarter), and a report on Retail Customers per class (currently served, disconnected, transferred), reasons for resorting to SOLR, service period, SOLR rate, pricing basis, and details on any customers reverting to the Captive Market.

faqs.section_title: Reportorial Requirements
faqs.question: What must every Retail Supplier report to the ERC quarterly?
faqs.answer: Its supply portfolio (contracted generation sources, capacity/energy); customer allocations; customer information (aggregated groups, retail category, meter/account numbers, DU franchise areas); pricing/contract details (kWh sales, revenues, average/contract prices, contract periods, pricing structure type); GEOP sales by RE technology; RAP details (number of groups, aggregated demand, member names/demand, contiguous area location); and complaint-handling statistics.

faqs.section_title: Reportorial Requirements
faqs.question: What financial documents must a Retail Supplier submit annually, and by when?
faqs.answer: A complete set of Audited Financial Statements (balance sheet, income statement, cash flow statement, notes), audit opinion, and management's responsibility statement, within one hundred fifty (150) calendar days from the end of the Financial Year (or as required by the BIR), including proof of the required Tangible Net Worth or AEAE.

faqs.section_title: Reportorial Requirements
faqs.question: What other periodic filings does a Retail Supplier need to make?
faqs.answer: A quarterly bank certification confirming available cash-security-deposit funds plus interest; an annual training report (due every January 31); an updated Mayor's/Business Permit (due every March 31); and annual review access to all executed/transacted RSCs (due every January 31) to confirm arm's-length dealing.

faqs.section_title: Reportorial Requirements
faqs.question: What must the CRB report to the ERC monthly?
faqs.answer: For CREM/GEOP: customer names, market category, supplier names, meter numbers, monthly registered demand and metered quantity, GEOP/eligible end-user switching counts and rates per DU franchise area, and switch type/date details. For RAP: aggregated group lists, supplier names, meter numbers, demand/quantity, and switching counts/rates.

faqs.section_title: Reportorial Requirements
faqs.question: How is "Completeness" scored for a Retail Supplier's reportorial submissions?
faqs.answer: Based on whether all required data and information under Module N was submitted; missing or incomplete data for any given report counts as non-compliance.

faqs.section_title: Reportorial Requirements
faqs.question: How is "Timeliness" scored for reportorial submissions?
faqs.answer: Based on whether the report was actually submitted and available by the deadline specified in the relevant Module; late submission (or none at all) counts as non-compliance.

faqs.section_title: Reportorial Requirements
faqs.question: Can the ERC require additional information beyond what is explicitly listed in Module N?
faqs.answer: Yes — the ERC may require such other information as it deems necessary or useful for market evaluation and monitoring, subject to appropriate confidentiality safeguards for proprietary or commercially sensitive data.

faqs.section_title: Reportorial Requirements
faqs.question: What happens to reportorial requirements during the transition period after the Omnibus Rules took effect?
faqs.answer: All Retail Suppliers, DUs, NSPs, and RMSPs continue to submit reportorial requirements in accordance with the existing procedures under ERC Resolution No. 09, Series of 2020, pending full transition to the CREM-MRS.

faqs.section_title: Reportorial Requirements
faqs.question: Why does the ERC require a supplier's PSAs to be reviewable, even though they are commercial contracts?
faqs.answer: To ascertain that these Power Supply Agreements were negotiated on an arms-length basis and do not violate market-control or anti-competitive rules, given the potential for cross-ownership and affiliate dealings in the sector. 15. Retail Supplier Good Standing and Scorecard Rating

faqs.section_title: Retail Supplier Good Standing and Scorecard Rating
faqs.question: What five parameters determine whether a Retail Supplier is "in Good Standing"?
faqs.answer: (a) its Retail Supplier Scorecard Rating; (b) compliance with reportorial requirements; (c) number of consumer complaints filed against it; (d) number of Show-Cause Orders issued against it; and (e) number of ERC Decisions ruled against it.

faqs.section_title: Retail Supplier Good Standing and Scorecard Rating
faqs.question: Who fills out the Retail Supplier Scorecard, and how often?
faqs.answer: Retail Customers, through the CREM-MRS, rate the services received from their Retail Supplier(s) once, at any point from one month before until one month after the RSC's expiration.

faqs.section_title: Retail Supplier Good Standing and Scorecard Rating
faqs.question: How is "Compliance with Reportorial Requirements" measured?
faqs.answer: Each report is scored on two dimensions — Completeness (all required data submitted) and Timeliness (submitted by the deadline) — with missing/incomplete/late/no submissions all counting as instances of non-compliance.

faqs.section_title: Retail Supplier Good Standing and Scorecard Rating
faqs.question: What does a "Show-Cause Order" indicate about a Retail Supplier?
faqs.answer: It signals that the ERC has determined a prima facie case exists against the supplier — an indicium of non-compliance with ERC rules — and is one of the scoring parameters for Good Standing.

faqs.section_title: Retail Supplier Good Standing and Scorecard Rating
faqs.question: What counts as a "Consumer Complaint" for scoring purposes?
faqs.answer: Formal written complaints and protests filed by a Retail Customer against its Retail Supplier — the existence (and resolution or lack thereof) of such complaints reflects the effectiveness of the supplier's Complaint Handling Procedures.

faqs.section_title: Retail Supplier Good Standing and Scorecard Rating
faqs.question: How much weight does the Retail Supplier Scorecard carry in the overall rating?
faqs.answer: 15% of the Total Rating, based on a range of initial ratings transmuted into grades: 100 to 90 scores 100 points; below 90 to 80 scores 75; below 80 to 70 scores 50; and below 70 scores 0.

faqs.section_title: Retail Supplier Good Standing and Scorecard Rating
faqs.question: How much weight do Completeness and Timeliness of reportorial submissions each carry?
faqs.answer: 15% each — Completeness is scored 100 (complete), 50 (incomplete), or 0 (no submission); Timeliness is scored 100 (on time), 50 (late), or 0 (no submission).

faqs.section_title: Retail Supplier Good Standing and Scorecard Rating
faqs.question: How is the Complaint Handling Procedure submission itself scored?
faqs.answer: Worth 10% of the total — 100 points if submitted on time, 50 if late, 0 if never submitted.

faqs.section_title: Retail Supplier Good Standing and Scorecard Rating
faqs.question: How are consumer complaints scored on the Good Standing scale?
faqs.answer: Worth 10% — zero complaints scores 100; one complaint scores 85; two to five complaints scores 75; more than five complaints scores 50.

faqs.section_title: Retail Supplier Good Standing and Scorecard Rating
faqs.question: How are Show-Cause Orders scored?
faqs.answer: Worth 10% — zero orders scores 100; one order scores 85; two to five orders scores 75; more than five orders scores 50.

faqs.section_title: Retail Supplier Good Standing and Scorecard Rating
faqs.question: Why does "Number of ERC Decisions Ruled Against the Supplier" carry the heaviest single weight (25%)?
faqs.answer: Because it is scored on an all-or-nothing basis (zero decisions scores 100; one or more scores 0), reflecting how seriously the ERC treats any adverse ruling as a marker of poor compliance, hence its outsized influence on the Total Rating.

faqs.section_title: Retail Supplier Good Standing and Scorecard Rating
faqs.question: What license renewal term does a "Very Satisfactory" Total Rating earn?
faqs.answer: Above 85% to 100% qualifies as "Very Satisfactory with complete compliance," recommending renewal with a ten (10)-year validity.

faqs.section_title: Retail Supplier Good Standing and Scorecard Rating
faqs.question: What happens if a Retail Supplier's Total Rating falls below 75%?
faqs.answer: It is rated "Failed," and the recommendation is non-renewal of its license.

faqs.section_title: Retail Supplier Good Standing and Scorecard Rating
faqs.question: What Total Rating range earns a five-year renewal instead of ten?
faqs.answer: 75% to 85%, rated "Satisfactory," recommending renewal with five (5)-year validity. 16. Miscellaneous Provisions — Sanctions, Confidentiality, and Dispute Resolution

faqs.section_title: Miscellaneous Provisions — Sanctions, Confidentiality, and Dispute Resolution
faqs.question: What happens if a court declares one provision of the Omnibus Rules invalid?
faqs.answer: Under the Separability Clause, the other unaffected parts or provisions remain in full force and effect — the invalidity of one module does not void the entire regulation.

faqs.section_title: Miscellaneous Provisions — Sanctions, Confidentiality, and Dispute Resolution
faqs.question: How many prior ERC resolutions did the Omnibus Rules repeal or amend?
faqs.answer: At least seventeen prior resolutions dating from 2005 to 2023 (covering RES licensing, code of conduct, SOLR, customer switching, contestability, and related transitory rules), plus any inconsistent provisions of the DSOAR.

faqs.section_title: Miscellaneous Provisions — Sanctions, Confidentiality, and Dispute Resolution
faqs.question: Can the ERC ever grant an exception to its own rules?
faqs.answer: Yes — where good cause appears, the ERC may allow an exception from any provision of the Omnibus Rules if doing so serves the public interest and is not contrary to law or other relevant rules and regulations.

faqs.section_title: Miscellaneous Provisions — Sanctions, Confidentiality, and Dispute Resolution
faqs.question: Through what channels must official notices under the Omnibus Rules be transmitted?
faqs.answer: In writing (personal service, registered mail, or reputable courier), by electronic mail, or through any other means of communication capable of time-stamping.

faqs.section_title: Miscellaneous Provisions — Sanctions, Confidentiality, and Dispute Resolution
faqs.question: How does the ERC treat confidential or proprietary information submitted by market participants?
faqs.answer: It affords such disclosed information strict confidentiality through appropriate protective measures, consistent with the Data Privacy Act of 2012, its IRR, and other National Privacy Commission issuances.

faqs.section_title: Miscellaneous Provisions — Sanctions, Confidentiality, and Dispute Resolution
faqs.question: What happens to a person or entity that acts as a Retail Supplier without a valid ERC license?
faqs.answer: It is subject to appropriate sanctions under existing laws, rules, and regulations, unless it falls under one of the specific exemptions (such as a duly Letter-authorized Local RES).

faqs.section_title: Miscellaneous Provisions — Sanctions, Confidentiality, and Dispute Resolution
faqs.question: Under what legal basis does the ERC impose fines and penalties for violations?
faqs.answer: The "Guidelines to Govern the Imposition of Administrative Sanctions in the Form of Fines and Penalties Pursuant to Section 46 of R.A. 9136," together with the penalties under Section 45 of EPIRA and any subsequent amendments, including possible license revocation or cancellation.

faqs.section_title: Miscellaneous Provisions — Sanctions, Confidentiality, and Dispute Resolution
faqs.question: Does the Anti-Pilferage Law (RA 7832) apply to Retail Customers as well as Captive Customers?
faqs.answer: Yes — the enforcement procedures under RA 7832 (penalizing electricity pilferage and theft of transmission materials) and its IRR, previously applicable to Captive Customers, are expressly extended to apply to Retail Customers as well.

faqs.section_title: Miscellaneous Provisions — Sanctions, Confidentiality, and Dispute Resolution
faqs.question: Which body has jurisdiction over disputes between Retail Market participants?
faqs.answer: The ERC has original and exclusive jurisdiction over all disputes between and among players and participants in the Retail Market, pursuant to Section 43(u) of EPIRA and existing jurisprudence.

faqs.section_title: Miscellaneous Provisions — Sanctions, Confidentiality, and Dispute Resolution
faqs.question: Must a dispute go through a Complaint Handling Procedure before reaching the ERC?
faqs.answer: Yes — parties must first exhaust the remedy under the Retail Supplier's ERC-submitted Complaint Handling Procedures before referring the dispute to the Commission, unless the parties have clearly agreed in writing (in the RSC) to another dispute-resolution mechanism.

faqs.section_title: Miscellaneous Provisions — Sanctions, Confidentiality, and Dispute Resolution
faqs.question: When do the Omnibus Rules take legal effect?
faqs.answer: Immediately upon their complete publication in a newspaper of general circulation or in the Official Gazette, unless a provision specifically states otherwise.

faqs.section_title: Miscellaneous Provisions — Sanctions, Confidentiality, and Dispute Resolution
faqs.question: Can penalties under the Omnibus Rules be combined with civil or criminal liability?
faqs.answer: Yes — administrative sanctions imposed by the ERC are separate from, and without prejudice to, whatever civil, criminal, or other legal liabilities may arise from the same violation under other applicable laws.

faqs.section_title: Miscellaneous Provisions — Sanctions, Confidentiality, and Dispute Resolution
faqs.question: If a Retail Supplier's RSC provides for an alternative dispute-resolution mechanism (e.g., arbitration), is that allowed?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the parties clearly agree upon it in writing and it is expressly stipulated in the RSC — but this does not override the ERC's original jurisdiction over regulatory disputes.

faqs.section_title: Miscellaneous Provisions — Sanctions, Confidentiality, and Dispute Resolution
faqs.question: Why does confidentiality protection matter so much for market participants under Module P5?
faqs.answer: Because Retail Suppliers, DUs, and other participants must submit extensive commercially sensitive data (pricing, contracts, financials) for regulatory monitoring, and without confidentiality safeguards this could be misused by competitors or harm legitimate business interests. 17. Transitory Provisions — Implementing the New Rules

faqs.section_title: Transitory Provisions — Implementing the New Rules
faqs.question: Which modules had to be complied with immediately upon the Omnibus Rules' effectivity?
faqs.answer: Module D (Participation of Eligible End-users), Module K (Reversion to Captive Market), Module L (Code of Conduct), and Module M (Magna Carta for Retail Customers) — these took effect right away for all NSPs, RMSPs, Retail Customers, and Retail Suppliers.

faqs.section_title: Transitory Provisions — Implementing the New Rules
faqs.question: How were pending RES License applications handled when the Omnibus Rules took effect?
faqs.answer: Applications filed after adoption of the Omnibus Rules are covered by the new rules; pending applications (including renewals) already in process continued under the prior licensing requirements of ERC Resolution No. 01, Series of 2011, and were issued five-year licenses upon approval.

faqs.section_title: Transitory Provisions — Implementing the New Rules
faqs.question: How much time did Retail Suppliers have to submit their Complaint Handling Procedures under the new rules?
faqs.answer: One (1) month from the effectivity of the Omnibus Rules, with immediate implementation and inclusion in all existing and future RSCs.

faqs.section_title: Transitory Provisions — Implementing the New Rules
faqs.question: What special transitional duty applied to RMSPs in Mindanao?
faqs.answer: Upon effectivity of the Omnibus Rules, RMSPs in Mindanao had to procure meters for prospective Retail Customers meeting the eligibility thresholds, subject to the Rules' provisions on settlement of meter installation and maintenance costs.

faqs.section_title: Transitory Provisions — Implementing the New Rules
faqs.question: What choice did residential condominium/building customers with a single revenue meter have to make under the transitory rules?
faqs.answer: Their Retail Suppliers had to notify the relevant homeowners' association (or authorized representative group) that it needed to issue a resolution stating its intention to remain in CREM or revert to captive status, exercisable at least three months before RSC expiry — failure to notify meant continued CREM participation by default.

faqs.section_title: Transitory Provisions — Implementing the New Rules
faqs.question: What deadline applied to Generation Companies supplying Directly Connected Customers?
faqs.answer: They had to secure a RES License within one (1) year from the effectivity of the Omnibus Rules.

faqs.section_title: Transitory Provisions — Implementing the New Rules
faqs.question: What deadline did the CRB/Market Operator have to operationalize Retail Aggregation?
faqs.answer: Sixty (60) calendar days from the effectivity of the Omnibus Rules to adapt and implement the necessary processes.

faqs.section_title: Transitory Provisions — Implementing the New Rules
faqs.question: What separate resolution did the ERC commit to issuing on metering cost recovery, and within what timeframe?
faqs.answer: A resolution rationalizing the cost recovery mechanism for procuring metering facilities across the different Customer Choice Programs and demand-management programs, within ninety (90) calendar days of the Omnibus Rules' effectivity.

faqs.section_title: Transitory Provisions — Implementing the New Rules
faqs.question: Has that promised metering cost-recovery resolution actually been issued yet?
faqs.answer: As reflected in the stakeholder comments on Resolution No. 22, Series of 2025, the ERC acknowledged that, due to complexities and roadblocks, the issuance has taken longer than the original ninety-day commitment, though it remains committed to completing it.

faqs.section_title: Transitory Provisions — Implementing the New Rules
faqs.question: What separate resolution did the ERC commit to on displaced contracted capacities?
faqs.answer: A resolution outlining the regulatory framework to address displaced contracted capacities/energy, within one hundred twenty (120) calendar days of the Omnibus Rules' effectivity.

faqs.section_title: Transitory Provisions — Implementing the New Rules
faqs.question: What can a DU do if customer migration to the Retail Market strands some of its bilateral supply contracts?
faqs.answer: It may provisionally implement mitigation measures — renegotiating power supply agreements, assigning excess contracted volumes to Retail Suppliers/Local RES/SOLR segments, or selling excess supply to the WESM — provided it demonstrates to the ERC that stranding exists and the measures achieve least-cost, reasonable rates for remaining captive customers.

faqs.section_title: Transitory Provisions — Implementing the New Rules
faqs.question: What report must DUs submit within thirty days of the Omnibus Rules' effectivity regarding demand and supply?
faqs.answer: A demand and supply assessment report covering total peak demand, number/demand of eligible end-users, existing Power Supply Agreements, eligible end-users intending to switch, and forecasted displaced contracted capacities for the coming year.

faqs.section_title: Transitory Provisions — Implementing the New Rules
faqs.question: How often must DUs update this demand and supply assessment report going forward?
faqs.answer: Every year, on or before December 15, consistent with Module

faqs.section_title: Getting Started — Understanding the Retail Electricity Market
faqs.question: 5. Q376. What happens to over/under recoveries in regulated charges that arose while a customer was still captive?
faqs.answer: They are confirmed by the ERC per its existing resolution on the matter (ERC Resolution No. 14, Series of 2022) and are refunded/collected as a separate bill line item through the Retail Supplier currently serving the customer. 18. Forms, Annexes, and Contract Templates

faqs.section_title: Forms, Annexes, and Contract Templates
faqs.question: What are the Annexes attached to the Omnibus Rules Resolution?
faqs.answer: Annex A is the Omnibus Rules text itself; Annexes B through D are RES/SOLR license checklists and business-plan outlines; Annexes E through H are contract templates (RSC, DWSA, Connection Agreement, SOLR Contract); Annex I is the SOLR application checklist; and Annexes J-1 to J-4 are quarterly/semi-annual reportorial forms.

faqs.section_title: Forms, Annexes, and Contract Templates
faqs.question: What is Annex E, and why would a beginner want to see it?
faqs.answer: Annex E is the template Retail Supply Contract (RSC) — reviewing it helps a new Retail Customer understand the standard structure, clauses, and language used in a real supply agreement before negotiating with a Retail Supplier.

faqs.section_title: Forms, Annexes, and Contract Templates
faqs.question: What does the RES License Checklist (Annex B-1) require regarding the applicant's email registration?
faqs.answer: Either the applicant's existing ERC Certificate of Email Registration (CER) number, or, if registration is pending, the reference number of the CER application — reflecting the ERC's move toward electronic applications under ERC Resolution No. 9, Series of 2020.

faqs.section_title: Forms, Annexes, and Contract Templates
faqs.question: What is Annex D (RES Form 3) used for?
faqs.answer: It is the prescribed outline for the RES/Local RES's Five-Year Business Plan, requiring an executive summary describing the applicant's current businesses, its parent/affiliate businesses, and (for new applicants) its reasons for entering the Retail Market.

faqs.section_title: Forms, Annexes, and Contract Templates
faqs.question: What does the Distribution Wheeling Service Agreement template (Annex F) cover?
faqs.answer: It is the template contract between a DU and a Retail Supplier (or Retail Customer, in dual billing) formalizing the terms for using the DU's distribution wires to deliver electricity to a Retail Customer.

faqs.section_title: Forms, Annexes, and Contract Templates
faqs.question: What is the Connection Agreement template (Annex G) for?
faqs.answer: It is the template agreement between a DU ("Company") and a customer covering the technical connection of the customer's facility to the distribution system — separate from, but often executed alongside, the DWSA and RSC.

faqs.section_title: Forms, Annexes, and Contract Templates
faqs.question: What is the Supplier of Last Resort Contract template (Annex H)?
faqs.answer: It is the standard contract format between a designated SOLR and a Retail Customer receiving Last Resort Supply, spelling out the SOLR's obligations and the customer's payment terms during the temporary backstop period.

faqs.section_title: Forms, Annexes, and Contract Templates
faqs.question: What is the SOLR application checklist (Annex I, SOLR Form 1) used for?
faqs.answer: It lists the documentary/legal requirements — starting with WESM Proof of Registration — that an entity must submit to be considered for designation as a Supplier of Last Resort.

faqs.section_title: Forms, Annexes, and Contract Templates
faqs.question: What information does the Retail Supplier's Quarterly Reportorial Form (Annex J-1) require about its supply portfolio?
faqs.answer: For each generation source: contracted capacity (MW), contracted energy (MWh), contract price (PhP/kWh), whether the source is an affiliate, resource type, and contract duration in years.

faqs.section_title: Forms, Annexes, and Contract Templates
faqs.question: What does the SOLR's Quarterly Reportorial Form (Annex J-3) require?
faqs.answer: Similar supply-portfolio details as the RES form — contracted capacity, contracted energy, contract price, contract duration, resource type, and whether the source is affiliated with the SOLR — but specific to the SOLR's own supply arrangements.

faqs.section_title: Forms, Annexes, and Contract Templates
faqs.question: What does the NSP's Semi-Annual Switching Compliance Report (Annex J-4) track?
faqs.answer: Retail Supplier and customer account/billing details, threshold levels, the date the NSP received notice of intent to switch, and the date the NSP submitted the required documents — used to measure the NSP's compliance with the twenty-day switching timeline.

faqs.section_title: Forms, Annexes, and Contract Templates
faqs.question: Why does the checklist approach matter for a first-time RES applicant?
faqs.answer: Because the ERC will only consider an application "filed" once all checklist items are complete, the Confirmation of Completeness Email (CCE) is issued, the application fee is paid, and official docketing occurs — missing even one document can delay the entire sixty-day review clock.

faqs.section_title: Forms, Annexes, and Contract Templates
faqs.question: Are these annex templates mandatory word-for-word, or just references?
faqs.answer: They generally serve as prescribed formats/starting templates; actual contracts must still conform to the minimum required provisions under the relevant Module (e.g., Module L12.2 for RSCs), though suppliers may add their own specific commercial terms. 19. Resolution No. 22, Series of 2025 — Lowering the Eligibility Threshold to 100kW

faqs.section_title: Resolution No. 22, Series of 2025 — Lowering the Eligibility Threshold to 100kW
faqs.question: What is Resolution No. 22, Series of 2025, in one sentence?
faqs.answer: It is the ERC Resolution, deliberated and approved on 30 October 2025, lowering the minimum eligibility threshold for CREM/RCOA and RAP from 500 kW to 100 kW average monthly peak demand, aligning it with the existing GEOP threshold.

faqs.section_title: Resolution No. 22, Series of 2025 — Lowering the Eligibility Threshold to 100kW
faqs.question: When does the new 100 kW threshold actually take effect?
faqs.answer: On 26 June 2026 — all End-users and Aggregated Groups meeting the 100 kW threshold who signified intent to switch on or before that date shall be switched to CREM/RCOA or RAP as applicable.

faqs.section_title: Resolution No. 22, Series of 2025 — Lowering the Eligibility Threshold to 100kW
faqs.question: Why did the ERC decide to lower the threshold specifically to 100 kW rather than some other level?
faqs.answer: To align the eligibility thresholds across all three Customer Choice Programs for consistency and regulatory coherence — the 100 kW level mirrors the threshold already implemented under GEOP since 2018.

faqs.section_title: Resolution No. 22, Series of 2025 — Lowering the Eligibility Threshold to 100kW
faqs.question: What market data did the ERC cite in deciding to lower the threshold?
faqs.answer: As of August 2025, 2,305 Retail Customers (about 61% of those meeting the 500 kW threshold) had already switched to CREM, and about 12,115 end-users nationwide fell within the 100 kW–499 kW range — a substantial pool that could benefit from lower thresholds.

faqs.section_title: Resolution No. 22, Series of 2025 — Lowering the Eligibility Threshold to 100kW
faqs.question: What milestone in the Retail Aggregation Program did the Resolution mention?
faqs.answer: The very first RAP switch occurred on 7 February 2025, when Manila Water's various facilities were aggregated to meet the 500 kW threshold; by August 2025, there were 37 Retail Aggregated Groups (RAGs) comprising 440 Aggregated Members with an equivalent demand of 30.95 MW.

faqs.section_title: Resolution No. 22, Series of 2025 — Lowering the Eligibility Threshold to 100kW
faqs.question: Did stakeholders unanimously support lowering the threshold to 100 kW immediately?
faqs.answer: No — while many supported the direction, several stakeholders (e.g., CEPALCO, MERALCO, RESA, PHILRECA, Aboitiz Power, FGEN) raised concerns about metering readiness, AMI deployment timelines, and requested a phased or transition-based approach rather than an abrupt, uniform rollout.

faqs.section_title: Resolution No. 22, Series of 2025 — Lowering the Eligibility Threshold to 100kW
faqs.question: What specific readiness concern did MERALCO raise about metering equipment procurement?
